title: Replace ternary facet-to-field chain with total, exported Record map
context: Round-2 review found fileEvidenceFor's open-ended ternary chain left the coverage boundary silently extensible: adding a facet to STATE_FACETS without guarding it would not cause a compile error, replicating the exact bug (unguarded `constraints`) that motivated this guard in the first place. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Replace the private ternary-chain function with an exported `FILE_EVIDENCE_FIELD: Record<StateFacet, string | null>` that exhaustively maps every StateFacet to its file-evidence field (or null). The function becomes a thin lookup into this map.
consequences: Adding a new facet to STATE_FACETS now causes a compile error if FILE_EVIDENCE_FIELD is not updated — the boundary is enforced at build time, not silently extensible
The facet-to-field mapping is now visible as a declaration, not buried in a conditional chain, making coverage decisions explicit and auditable

Tests can assert the mapping directly in isolation, replacing the prior 'vacuous' test (receipts' own `scope` object field made Array.isArray pass regardless of correctness) with exhaustive positive and negative cases
Null entries explicitly document which facets intentionally carry no file evidence, preventing confusion about whether an entry is missing or just not needed
alternatives_rejected: Keep the ternary chain and rely on code review / linter rules to catch missing entries — still silent and procedure-dependent, not enforced at compile time
Use TypeScript's exhaustiveness checking (`never` at the call site) without exporting the map — would catch errors at the use site but prevent independent testing of the boundary
Keep the map private and only test via live misroute behavior — loses the ability to pinpoint mapping bugs without probing the entire guard's behavior
